item.description: NPR's Joel Rose talks with Oregon Governor Tina Kotek about the shooting at Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, Oregon.

item.title: Student protests widen into greater social unrest in France
item.description: Hundreds of protests took place in cities across France. Most of them were peaceful but some turned chaotic and violent.

item.title: Iowa's vote in midterms may help determine balance of power in Congress
item.description: Iowa Public Radio's Natalie Krebs reports on how Iowa - a state that reliably votes Republican for president - has some competitive races for Republicans in November, which could help determine the balance of power in Congress.

item.title: Biking along the Great American Rail-Trail
item.description: Organizers hope to connect more than 150 existing rail-trails, greenways and other paths spanning more than 3,700 miles across America. NPR's Joel Rose checks on their progress in western Pennsylvania, West Virginia and Ohio.

item.title: How public bathrooms reflect America's inequality
item.description: Public restrooms are scarce in cities across the U.S. It's a topic historian and Temple University professor Bryant Simon writes about in his new book 'For Customers Only: Public Bathrooms and the Making of American Inequality.'

item.title: Mayor of Bend shares how her community is doing after elementary school shooting
item.description: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Mayor of Bend Melanie Kebler about how the community is grieving the three children and teacher who were killed in a shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School on Thursday.

item.title: Here's what experts say about the civilian intervention in the Bend school shooting
item.description: An armed bystander stopped a shooting at a school in Bend, Ore. We talk with experts about how rarely an armed civilian ends an attack like this and how gun rights groups are responding.

item.title: 'Where is Austin Tice': NPR series investigates a journalist's disappearance in Syria
item.description: A new investigative series by NPR looks into the real life missing person case of American journalist Austin Tice, who disappeared in Syria over a decade ago.
